verdicts.reason: A: the CITRINE wordmark sits below the headline, which flips the brand-then-message order. The 'Find a Store' button is tiny, with barely legible text, and its left edge doesn't line up with the centered headline. B has the same order problem and a worse CTA: an even smaller pill stranded at the bottom right, far from the copy and almost unreadable, so it reads as an afterthought.

A gives the banner a clear left-to-right read: product, then headline, then a properly sized CTA on the right. Its flaws are the brand wordmark still sitting under the headline and the CTA running into the green circle at the right edge. B's CTA is a tiny pill tucked under the headline at the bottom edge, with near-illegible text and weak alignment, so the action is buried.

A shrinks the Quillbrook bag, the key product image, to an unreadable icon beside a tiny CTA at the bottom right. That loses the original's main visual and leaves a big empty left side with a ragged headline and wordmark. B keeps the product prominent, but its CTA is tiny and nearly illegible, it is misaligned with the centered headline, and the wordmark sits below the headline.
